opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, write is within policy; recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max; recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent's note states Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only if they have advanced security training; with basic training the maximum allowed level is read. The requested write exceeds this maximum, so grant the maximum of read. (Note: HR's note conflicts on employment type, but I'm granting the more conservative level supported by the Security DB facts.)

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

HR says full-time Payroll Specialist → write is allowed (full-time up to write, and role owns the system, so even admin allowed, but requested write, so grant write).

Security says contractor with basic training → contractor max is read (no advanced training), so grant read.
